logline: Three working-class students enter Las Encinas, Spain's most exclusive private school, and the collision with old money ends in murder.

renewal.note: Ended with Season 8 released July 26, 2024; Netflix confirmed no Season 9.

bollymeter.basis: Critics identified the class-collision premise as sharper than typical teen drama, and the murder-mystery structure gave the lurid plotting a backbone that kept it more than gossip.

pull_quotes.text: A wickedly plotted Spanish teen drama that uses class warfare to give its salacious thrills genuine bite.

seasons.review_body: Season 1 landed as a sharper, more politically conscious entry into the teen drama genre than its premise suggested. Three scholarship kids dropped into Spain's most elite private school - the class resentment was the real engine, murder just the delivery mechanism. The flash-forward structure, jumping between police interviews and the events leading to the crime, imposed a discipline on the chaos. Critics called it propulsive and noted the young cast handled heavy material with conviction. Creators Darío Madrona and Carlos Montero built something that operated simultaneously as pulpy entertainment and pointed social commentary.

episode_reviews.title: Bienvenidos
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The three working-class arrivals at Las Encinas are introduced against a cold-open flash-forward that reveals a death before a name. The social hierarchies are drawn fast and sharp - wealth as armor, newness as vulnerability.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The interrogation flash-forward that opens the series: we know someone dies before we know who anyone is.

critic_note.text: Uses class tension to elevate a teen murder mystery above its genre defaults.

episode_reviews.title: Polo
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The season resolves its murder mystery with a reveal that recontextualizes nearly every prior episode. The writing is careful enough that the answer feels inevitable rather than cheap - the class dynamics that opened the show are the same ones that close it.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The revelation of who died and how flips the moral weight of the entire season.

critic_note.text: A finale that pays off its structural precision with real emotional consequence.

bollymeter.basis: 92% on Rotten Tomatoes; critics found the show confident in its second outing, expanding its canvas without losing the tight class-war tension of the first season.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 deepened the ensemble and introduced new scholarship students without losing the original trio's central tension. The murder-mystery format held, the class commentary remained pointed, and the show's willingness to put its characters in genuinely ugly situations separated it from safer teen fare. At 92% critic score from 12 reviews, the critical reception was strong if narrower than the audience footprint. The show understood its own voice by now - sharp, salacious, structurally disciplined - and delivered.
seasons.season_over_season: Slightly less impact than the debut by virtue of surprise deficit, but arguably more confident storytelling.

bollymeter.basis: 100% on Rotten Tomatoes from 10 critics - a small sample but consensus that this was the show peaking; the original cast's arc resolved with real weight.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 closed the original chapter of Las Encinas with the critical consensus at its warmest - the show at its narrative sharpest. The founding cast's arcs paid off, the class politics reached a conclusion that felt both inevitable and earned, and the writing team knew how to end a story. In hindsight, this was the natural series finale. The decision to continue with a largely new cast in Season 4 is understandable commercially; artistically, the original trilogy ends here.
seasons.season_over_season: The best of the original trilogy - tighter plotting, more satisfying character payoff, and a finale that functions as a proper ending.

bollymeter.basis: Critics noted the new cast struggled to recreate the original's chemistry and the class-war premise felt diluted; audience scores dropped noticeably.

seasons.review_body: Season 4 opened the post-original-cast era with a largely new ensemble and a creative reset that critics received with muted enthusiasm. The Las Encinas formula remained - new money, old secrets, murder framing device - but the irreplaceable dynamic of the first three seasons' core trio was gone. Watchable for fans already invested in the world, but no longer essential television.
seasons.season_over_season: A pronounced step down from Season 3; the new cast needed more time to build audience investment before carrying the show's structural weight.

bollymeter.basis: 80% on Rotten Tomatoes but a thin sample; critics noted the show repeating formula without conviction.

seasons.review_body: Season 5 continued Las Encinas with another new intake of characters and diminishing critical attention. The 80% score from just five reviews signals the show had moved from a critical conversation piece to background content. The writing remained competent, the production values unchanged, but the urgency of the original had been fully spent.
seasons.season_over_season: Stable but inert - the show is running on institutional momentum rather than creative drive.

bollymeter.basis: Widely flagged as the franchise's nadir: critics and long-time fans judged the formula exhausted and the once-sharp class commentary reduced to shock for its own sake. BollyAI marks it a SKIP.

seasons.review_body: Season 6 is where critical patience visibly ran out: reviews skewed overwhelmingly negative at a formula the show was no longer refreshing. The original class-war sharpness had been replaced by recycled drama with characters the audience had no reason to care about. A harsh landing for a show that opened to genuine acclaim.
seasons.season_over_season: A total critical collapse - the 100-point swing from Season 3 to Season 6 is one of the steepest critical falls in modern streaming history.

bollymeter.basis: Partial critical recovery; a small sample of reviews were mixed-to-positive, suggesting the show found its footing again in limited respects.

seasons.review_body: Season 7 represented a partial recovery from the Season 6 nadir. The small sample of available reviews trended mixed-to-positive. The show remained far below its original peak, but the writers appeared to have absorbed criticism and made some adjustments. For completionists only.
seasons.season_over_season: Slight improvement on Season 6 - the 0% was unsustainable, and the writing made modest corrections.

bollymeter.basis: The series finale season. Critics and audience gave it moderate marks; it ended the show without returning to original-era quality, but gave the fanbase a proper conclusion.

seasons.review_body: Season 8 closed Elite's run with a finale season that critics received politely rather than warmly. The show had long since exhausted its critical capital; this was an exercise in tying off threads for a still-sizable fanbase. The ending was clean enough. Six years is a reasonable run for a teen drama built on a high-concept premise, and the original three seasons remain genuinely good television regardless of where the later seasons went.
seasons.season_over_season: A dignified close - not a return to form, but a proper ending rather than a cancellation cliff.
